quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on a green light must let oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on a green light must let oncoming traffic pass first.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to clear before turning.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them in return.
Make sure they know you do not approve of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and put distance between your vehicle and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
Only if the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask you to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they are crossing against a red light or being careless.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light is a warning. Slow down and continue with caution.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights on, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights, sirens, or other warning devices, you must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will be merging into your lane from the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Merging traffic.
Prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that a side road is coming up and traffic may enter from it.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the shoulder with no children in it.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane highway when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing and/or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign means a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right and then left.
The road ahead curves left and then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right and then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming dangers. This sign warns you that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move as soon as one train passes. Wait until you have a clear view of all tracks. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUI arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and liquor
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving ability. This includes alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and prescription or over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed in both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic.

questions.question: When may you pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk?

options.text: When the vehicle does not accelerate quickly after the pedestrian leaves.
When the pedestrian is directly in front of the vehicle.
When you cannot see a pedestrian.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. The law assumes any stopped vehicle is waiting for a pedestrian to cross, even if you cannot see one.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.
Busy sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crossing ahead. Watch for people crossing your path. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What must you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely and check for pedestrians and traffic. Wait for the intersection to clear before moving.

questions.question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You can leave without trying to find the owner.
Find the owner or leave a note.
Wait by the vehicle until the owner returns.
Call a tow truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find the owner or leave a note.
questions.explanation: If you hit an unattended vehicle, try to find the owner and notify police. If you cannot find the owner, leave a note with your name, phone number, and license plate number.

questions.question: What do highways use to direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows show which lanes to use. They tell you to go straight or turn.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.
Merging traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill slope is coming.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. This helps you control your car, stay in your lane, and react to surprises.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is loose.
Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Is hidden beneath the seat.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from operating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear its siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road right away and stop.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive with your flashers on.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: You may park or stop along the shoulder of the freeway:

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be traveling at a speed slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when approaching them from behind. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Signal before going any further.
Slow down and yield for trains.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must let them pass first.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cellular phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. You need to focus all your attention on driving. Any other task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb when parking uphill. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, ____ has the right-of-way.

options.text: The funeral procession
A pedestrian
Another driver
A bicyclist

questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. Once the first vehicle enters an intersection, all other vehicles in the procession may follow through, even if traffic lights say to stop.

questions.question: When meeting a car with blinding headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car is coming toward you with high beams on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: Under no circumstances.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Your chances of being in a collision start to increase after consuming:

options.text: Four alcoholic drinks.
Three alcoholic drinks.
Two alcoholic drinks.
One alcoholic drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink increases your crash risk. No amount of alcohol is safe when driving, regardless of how long you have been driving.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle stopped on the side of the road, drivers should:

options.text: Increase their speed.
Move to another lane or slow down.
Pull off the road behind the stationary vehicle.
Move to the lane closest to the stationary vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: The Move Over Law protects emergency workers, tow truck drivers, sanitation workers, and utility workers on the roadside. You must move away from them or slow down to at least 20 mph below the speed limit.

questions.question: While backing, you should:

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Turn your head to look out the rear window. Mirrors and sensors alone are not enough because children and small objects are hard to see.

questions.question: You come to an intersection that is blocked by other traffic. You should:

options.text: Go slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
Sound your horn to make the cars move up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through it. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: When may you honk your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound it to alert other drivers.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle?

options.text: On an incline.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
An upcoming curve in the road.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road ahead curves to the right.

questions.question: If you see a roadway covered with water, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through until the water seems too deep.
Drive through. The water is unlikely to be very deep.
Turn around and find another route.
Walk into the water to check its depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through flooded roads. Turn around and find another way. You cannot tell how deep the water is or how strong the current is. Your vehicle could be swept away or submerged.

questions.question: Night driving is:

options.text: Less dangerous than day driving.
No more or less dangerous than day driving.
More dangerous than day driving.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than day driving.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. Also, more tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: Strong black coffee will keep them awake.
They can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
Opening a window and turning up the radio will keep them alert.
Only older drivers get drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly they seem drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough. Drowsy drivers are still a danger.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually to let them pass.
Never slow down suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If a car tailgates you and a right lane is open, move over. If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear, then slow down gradually. This encourages the tailgater to pass. Never stop suddenly as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beams.
High beams.
Any lights work the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Excessive speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Excessive speed.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you drive too fast, your tires lose grip and the car slides on a film of water. This is hydroplaning.
